body.en:
Question B-007-003-004.

Why the correct answer is right: A skip zone begins where the ground wave no longer provides useful reception and ends at the first ionosphere-refracted return point. Those two boundaries define the gap.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "a zone of silence caused by lost sky waves": This blames missing sky waves but leaves out the ground-wave boundary and the first return point that define the zone.
- sourceIndex 2: "a zone between any two refracted waves": A gap between later hops is not the standard first skip-zone definition.
- sourceIndex 3: "a zone between the antenna and the return of the first refracted wave": The area near the antenna can still have ground-wave coverage, so the zone does not begin at the antenna.
